doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

chapter: The Sound of Jazz and Lester Young
title: Lester Young and Billie Holiday in the control room
summary: A clip plays; Hentoff recalls Lester Young being unwell and the emotional Billie Holiday and Lester Young moment.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well I sometimes fantasize about getting in a time machine and going back. I’m like really jealous of the moments you’ve had. And one of them was, I actually —
I was in the control room. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
Oh God, is that perfect or what?

Billie came in right after. You know the background of that was Lester was not feeling well. He was supposed to be in one of the big band sections with the all-time sax section: Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, I forget who else we had there. And he just — I said look, you don’t have to do that, and when you do the small combo thing with Billie, you can just sit down. And then she came on in a circle with Roy Eldridge and Lester etcetera. He got up and in the control room, people, as this was unfolding, had tears in their eyes. It was such a moment. Because they were looking at each other, as Lester played. And they had been very close and then not so close, and it was so personal and so intimate, and I was so glad we got that for the ages, if anybody ever wants to see it again.
